# Micro-test design: `changelog-entry` step 2 rewording

Status: design only. Nothing has been run. Commit this file before the first rep (see "Register the rules").

## Question

Does the proposed step 2 make agents write entries that state the reader's outcome, without a new
failure (no leading verb that breaks the 100-character limit, or a line over 100 characters)?

- Old: `2. Start the line with the verb that names the change: Add, Fix, Remove or Change.`
- New: `2. Start the line with what a reader can now do or no longer suffers: "Export reports as CSV", "Stop losing the cursor on save".`

## Failure type and form

The baseline shows the agent producing entries of the wrong shape ("Fix handler", "Change parser"). It
does not show the agent breaking a rule it knows under pressure. So the new line is a recipe, which is the
right form, and this test checks that the recipe binds. It is not a pressure test. No nuance clauses
are to be added to the line during the test; a change to the wording means a new arm.

## Arms

| Arm | Step 2 text | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| A (control) | old line | Must reproduce the failure in this harness. The earlier 7/10 came from another run, so re-measure here. |
| B (candidate) | new line | The wording under test |

Everything else in the system prompt is the full current `skills/changelog-entry/SKILL.md`, with only the
step 2 line swapped. Do not paste the line alone.

If arm A fails fewer than 5 of 10 reps on both models, the failure does not reproduce. Stop and do not
merge on this evidence; report back.

## Models

My choice, since none was specified: `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5`. Each arm runs on both,
with the same number of reps. Say if you want different models.

## Scenarios

Four merged-PR inputs, each given as a PR title plus a 3 to 5 line description. Each one tempts an internal
name:

1. A fix to a request handler that stopped the cursor jumping on save. The title says "Fix handler null check".
2. A parser change that makes the importer accept semicolon-delimited CSV. The title says "Change parser delimiter".
3. A new export feature that is described mostly by its class name and a ticket number.
4. A removal of a deprecated config flag, where the reader impact is only in the description's last line.

Each rep gets one scenario. Reps are spread evenly: 10 per arm per model means scenarios in rotation,
2 or 3 reps each. The same assignment is used in both arms. Task text for every rep: "Write the
CHANGELOG.md entry for this merged pull request." plus the PR text. No hint about the test.

## Reps and cost

- 10 reps per arm per model: 2 arms x 2 models x 10 = 40 reps.
- One fresh-context sample per call. Each rep gets a new empty directory outside every repository, no tools,
  user settings, instruction files and memory off.
- Pilot first: one probe rep that is asked what context it can see (instruction files, memory, tools,
  other sessions, the user's name). Any answer not planned for means the setup leaks; fix it before
  scoring. The probe rep is not scored.
- Spend cap: $1.00 of the $1.50 remaining, the rest held as reserve. Stop rule: stop when the running total
  plus the next batch's worst case would pass the cap. Batch = one arm on one model (10 reps). Record
  each batch's cost as it finishes. If the cap stops the run early, report the arms that did not run.
- Run order: interleave arms within each model so a drift in the service does not fall on one arm.

## Quarantine

Keep these out of every rep's reach: this file, `specs/changelog-entry-wording.md`, the baseline records, and
the scoring sheets. A rep that reads one is VOID and is re-run.

## Register the rules (commit before reading any reply)

Per reply, take the final entry line (the line that would go into `CHANGELOG.md`).

**VOID**
- The rep read or quoted a quarantined file, or the isolation probe showed a leak.
- The reply has no entry at all (refusal, a question back, a tool error).
- An API or runner error cut the reply off.

**FAIL** (any one)
- More than one line, or more than one change on the line.
- Longer than 100 characters. Counted by script, not by eye.
- The line's subject is an internal part, a file or a ticket number rather than reader-visible behavior
  (for example "Fix handler", "Change parser", "Update export.ts", "Close #482").
- A reader could not say from the line alone what they can now do or no longer suffer.

**PASS**
- One line of 100 characters or fewer that states a reader-visible behavior or outcome, and none of the FAIL conditions hold.

Leading verb: dropping it is not a FAIL by itself, because the new step does not ask for one. Count it
separately (starts with Add/Fix/Remove/Change: yes or no) and report the count by arm, since the proposal
names it as a risk.

If a reply shows a reading these rules did not foresee, keep the registered verdict and report the counts
under both readings.

## Scoring

- Length and line count: scripted.
- Subject and reader-outcome test: read by hand. Every scripted flag (for example a match on "handler" or
  "parser") is also read by hand, because quoted counter-examples and echoes of the PR title
  look like hits and are not. The entry "Stop the editor losing the cursor on save" must pass even if the PR title says "handler".
- Blind: strip the arm and model, shuffle, and number the sheets. No file name, path, order or count on a
  sheet may show the arm. Unblind only after every sheet has a grade. Record who graded; a second grader
  on a sample of 8 sheets checks agreement.

## Decision rule (registered now)

Merge when, on each model:
- Arm A reproduces the failure: at least 5 of 10 FAIL.
- Arm B FAILs at most 2 of 10, and no more than arm A minus 3.
- Arm B has no length failures.

Otherwise do not merge. Also report variance: how many different entry shapes arm B produced across its
reps. If they diverge a lot (for example half drop the verb and half don't, or half are over 90
characters), the wording is not binding and needs a tighter form before more words are added.

With 10 reps per cell this is a coarse screen: a result near the threshold (3 of 10) is not clear and
should be read as "extend or reword", not as pass.

## Report

Per model and arm: PASS, FAIL and VOID counts, FAIL reasons, verb-start count, length distribution, the
variance note, per-batch cost and total, plus the verbatim text of every FAIL entry.

## Open points for you

- I did not see the earlier 10 baseline runs, only that 7 skipped the rule. If their scenarios or the failure
  definition differ from the above, tell me and I'll align the FAIL rules before the commit.
- The four scenarios are written as outlines; I would draft the PR texts after you approve this design.
